Hi Samantha / Acme team,

Thanks again for confirming the booth footprint and lead-flow method. Before we finalize the badge scanner config, legal asked that we lock the exact opt-in wording and confirm the HubSpot field mapping so we avoid duplicate contacts and accidental auto-merge.

Attached: privacy-checklist.pdf (short checklist), hubspot-field-map.xlsx (proposed field mapping), consent-sample.txt (booth verbatim).

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm Acme will capture the explicit checkbox labeled: "I consent to receive marketing communications from Redwood Inference and event partners. Learn more at redwood.com/privacy"?
- We want a daily CSV export (UTC) from the scanner system with a field indicating explicit_consent=true/false. Is that possible?
- HubSpot mapping: we propose writing raw badge data to a temporary import list and using a dedupe key of email + event_id. Please see the attached sheet and flag any column names that don't match your export.

Timeline: we need final wording by Friday EOD (10/30) to get the scanners pre-configured. If there are compliance constraints (EU data subjects), call that out and we'll switch to local retention.

Thanks — looping in Ben and Marissa for ops & partner coordination.

Hey all — quick confirm from sales-ops: HubSpot import does not support a compound dedupe rule (email+event_id) out of the box for the hosted account we use. We have two practical options:

1) Pre-process the nightly CSV and generate a synthetic dedupe_key: lower(email) + '|' + event_id, and import using that custom property as the dedupe key. (requires a tiny lambda to run on the SFTP consumer)
2) Import raw and run a scheduled dedupe job after import using workflows. That's riskier for race conditions and duplicates during the event.

I recommend option 1 for reliability. I can prototype the lambda and coordinate access to the SFTP. If Samantha can confirm the exact column names and timestamp format, I can have a PoC ready by Friday.

Connor OBrien
